title: Choose the visual world for LaMP
question: The roll assigned Station Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Station Board
options.lineage: South Asian railway timetables and yellow station name boards
options.thesis: The next 30 days of money, read like a departures board.
options.viewport: Green header, a yellow next-stop board reading 'Short BDT 19,000 on 26 Oct', then upcoming money stops in timetable rows.
options.risk: Becomes a train costume if boards appear everywhere; the board must stay the one signature move.

raised.raise: Every day's balance is checked against the cash buffer, so no plan can overflow the till.
Every headline number opens the invoice or sales page it came from.
Suppliers keep a fixed plate (name, due day, terms) in one stable order on every screen.
The sticky header names the date span in view, recomputed as the list scrolls.
The cash line is drawn to true time scale: the gap between stops is real days.
All money is set in tabular figures, right-aligned to the taka.

options.label: Carton & Strip
options.lineage: medicine cartons and blister strips on the pharmacy shelf
options.thesis: Every figure stamped like a batch code on a medicine carton.
options.viewport: White screen with a coloured band per section; due and expiry dates printed as inkjet stamps.
options.risk: Familiar: closest to how pharmacy and health apps already look, so less memorable.

options.label: Cassette J-card
options.thesis: Money in and money out as side A and side B of one folded card.
options.viewport: Income as side A, outgoings as side B, running totals right-aligned.
options.case: Fuses poorly: owners don't identify with mixtapes, and handwriting blurs exact taka figures.
options.kept: Capacity discipline: a side must never overflow the tape.
options.risk: Handwritten numbers undermine trust in money.

options.label: Monochrome product page
options.thesis: Every claim paired with the interface detail that proves it.
options.viewport: Claim and proof pairs down a neutral page.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a marketing form, cold and bank-like on a working screen.
options.risk: Reads as a generic startup template.

options.label: Character goods catalog
options.thesis: Suppliers as a ranked roster of characters.
options.viewport: A grid of supplier mascots ranked by spend.
options.case: Fuses poorly: toy-like, which the owner explicitly rejected for money.
options.kept: A finite roster with fixed personal fields in a stable order.

options.label: Lexicon page
options.thesis: Accounts set as a dense reference page with guide words.
options.viewport: Tight text columns with guide words naming the range in view.
options.case: Fuses poorly: too dense and bookish for a phone at a busy counter.
options.kept: Guide words naming the span you are inside.
options.risk: Unreadable in bright light at phone size.

options.label: Dance notation
options.thesis: Cash events as blocks whose length is their duration.
options.viewport: A vertical staff with money events rising through time.
options.case: Fuses poorly: an unfamiliar notation owners would have to learn.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Cash as a strobing barcode field.
options.viewport: Dense monospace columns over a barcode field.
options.case: Fuses poorly: cold, dense and art-gallery, the opposite of a counter tool.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean fintech dashboard, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Balance card, a line chart and a list of upcoming payments.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every finance app, and close to the bank look the owner rejected.
